frontier.hypothesis: Canonical-asm authorization under the GTE-leaf carve-out remains the disposition, and session 7 upgrades the argument from 'no C spelling found' to 'the target is not a fixed point of this compiler'.
frontier.mechanism: Two orthogonal impossibility proofs now stand. H1: reorg.c:730-735 stop_search_p halts fill_simple_delay_slots at any asm insn, so the target's delay-slot ctc2 - an opcode with no C analog - can never be placed there from C. H16: reload1.c:3606 order_regs_for_reload requires $2,$3,$5,$6,$7 to be in regs_ever_live for the eight values to land on $t0..$t7, and the target's own 17 instructions mention none of those five, so the shipped register allocation cannot arise from the shipped instruction stream. Precedent is in hand and citable: func_80052B44, src/text1b.c:10995, inline_asm_canonical.txt:340, authorized 2026-07-27 for the identical construct one function later in the same file.
frontier.next_probe: Operator step, or a session holding authority over inline_asm_canonical.txt: apply memory/grind/func_80052B00/candidate.c over src/text1b.c:10969-10994, add the canonical entry, run `retire func_80052B00` (drops regfix.txt:3411) and `verify-oracle`. The disposition call belongs to the driver/owner; a grind session in a non-escalation modality must not self-authorize it.

frontier.hypothesis: If the canonical disposition is ever REFUSED, memory/grind/func_80052B00/best_pure_c_fused8_floor17.c - not the pinned HEAD body - is what should ship, because it strictly reduces the cheat surface. Session 7 confirms no cheaper honest form exists.
frontier.mechanism: The HEAD body needs eight register asm("$N") pins PLUS regfix.txt:3411 to byte-match. The fused body is pin-free and already correct in opcodes, order and offsets; only the GPR names and the delay-slot move remain as build-time paperwork. Every form that scores below 17 does so by changing the function's contract (fake parameters, fake return type, stores past the array) and is banked under rejected/.
frontier.next_probe: Operator step (a grind session may not touch these surfaces): splice the fused body into src/text1b.c, measure `sandbox func_80052B00` WITHOUT --disable all to see what the enabled rule set achieves, determine the minimal rule set that reaches byte-match, and run a full `verify-oracle`.

frontier.hypothesis: The single acknowledged loophole in H16 - a construct whose insn exists at reload entry but is deleted by a post-reload pass, setting regs_ever_live at zero emitted cost.
frontier.mechanism: regs_ever_live is latched before reload runs, so occupancy established by an insn that flow2 or jump2 later deletes would be free. Every construct measured in sessions 1-7 either emits the instruction (ctlE, ctlI, occ3/occ5) or fails to set occupancy at all (unused params in s6 ctlF/ctlG, varargs homing in s7 ctlJ).
frontier.next_probe: Low expected value, recorded so nobody re-derives it and nobody overclaims the proof: grep the post-reload passes in tools/gcc-2.7.2 for their deletion conditions and try to manufacture a C source that hits one. Even a hit leaves H1's delay slot, so the floor still could not reach 0 - do NOT spend a session on this ahead of the disposition in frontier item 1.
